findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs, not group IDs
findings.body:
In the V2 implementation the authorization `Resource` created for a group uses the *group id as the resource name* (see `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`/`getOrCreateResource`), while `Resource#getId()` is the unrelated internal UUID of the authz resource. This method adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set and also passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)`, which resolves the group via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`.

Consequences:
1. `hasPermission` never finds the per-group resource for the id it is given, so it always falls through to the "all groups" resource-type resource - the per-group evaluation intended here does not happen.
2. The returned set is consumed as a set of *group ids*: `UsersResource.searchForUser` puts it in `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (restricting the user query to members of those groups) and `UsersResource.getUsersCount` passes it to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`. Because the ids are authz resource ids, they match no group, so an admin holding an all-groups `view-members`/`manage-members` permission gets zero users and a count of 0 from `/users` and `/users/count`.

The V1 implementation deliberately strips the resource-name prefix (`resource.getName().substring(RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX.length())`) to produce group ids; V2 should use `groupResource.getName()`. Note also that resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` never get `setType(...)`, so `findByType(server, "Groups", ...)` only returns the single "Groups" resource-type resource, never the per-group resources - the loop can therefore never enumerate individual groups. No test covers this code path (the existing tests pass via the per-user `canView(user)` filter).

findings.title: canManage() grants manage when only the VIEW scope is permitted
findings.body: `canManage()` evaluates `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` - i.e. it returns `true` when the caller only has the `view` scope on the "all groups" resource (looks like a copy/paste from `canView()` two methods above). `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` calls `auth.groups().requireManage()`, so an administrator who was granted only a read-only all-groups permission can create top-level groups. This is a privilege escalation; the check must only accept `MANAGE`. The new Javadoc added to `GroupPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` documents the same wrong semantics and should be fixed as well.

findings.title: NPE when the "Groups" resource-type resource does not exist
findings.body: When no per-group resource is found, the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` and immediately dereferences the result via `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and later `resource.getScopes()`, without a null check. `getResourceTypeResource` returns `null` whenever the resource named "Groups" is absent for the admin-permissions client. This is reachable for any realm where admin permissions were enabled before this change: `AdminPermissionsSchema.init()` returns early when the admin permissions client already exists, and there is no migration that adds the newly introduced "Groups" resource/scopes to existing resource servers. Any group-related permission check in such a realm will then fail with a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) instead of simply denying access.

findings.title: Group deletion breaks when both FGAP v1 and v2 features are enabled
findings.body: `MgmtPermissionsV2` now overrides `groups()` to return `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled(...)`/`isPermissionsEnabled(...)` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (registered whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled) handles `GroupModel.GroupRemovedEvent` by calling `management(session, realm).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false)`, and `management(...)` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` as soon as `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. With both features enabled, deleting any group in any realm therefore throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, failing the delete request (500) and aborting the transaction. The same override also makes `GET/PUT /groups/{id}/management/permissions` fail with 500 instead of operating on the v1 permission model. Either the listener/endpoints must be gated to the v1 implementation, or these methods must degrade gracefully (no-op/false) in v2.

findings.title: All-groups permissions are silently ignored for any group that has its own permission
findings.body: `hasPermission` only falls back to the "all groups" resource when no resource exists for the specific group. A per-group resource is created as soon as *any* group-scoped permission references that group (`AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource`). Because per-group resources are created without a resource type, type-based policy evaluation does not apply either. Result: once an admin creates, say, a `manage-membership` permission for group G, all broader all-groups permissions (e.g. `view`, `view-members`) stop applying to G, so an administrator who could previously view G loses that access as a side effect of an unrelated permission being created for G. The scopes granted at the resource-type level should be evaluated in addition to, not instead of, the group-specific resource.

findings.title: getResourceName does not handle the new Groups resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` only special-cases `USERS` (returning "All users" or the username). For the newly added `Groups` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource` (they are created with name = group id and no display name). Admin API/console responses that list the resources of a group scope permission will therefore show `null`/empty instead of the group name or "All groups", unlike the Users resource type. The method needs a `GROUPS` branch resolving the group by id (and a name for the all-groups resource).

findings.title: switch over resourceType throws NPE for a null resource type
findings.body: The previous implementation used `USERS.getType().equals(resourceType)` chains, which tolerated a `null` `resourceType` and ended up throwing the descriptive `IllegalStateException("Could not map resource object ...")`. `switch (resourceType)` on a `String` throws `NullPointerException` when the argument is null, which surfaces as an opaque HTTP 500 for any caller that reaches `getOrCreateResource` without a resource type. Add an explicit null check that raises `ModelValidationException` (consistent with `throwExceptionIfResourceTypeOrScopesNotProvided`).

findings.title: Incorrect Javadoc on new GroupPermissionEvaluator methods
findings.body: Two of the newly added Javadoc blocks are wrong: `requireManageMembers(GroupModel)` is documented as "Throws ForbiddenException if {@link #canManageMembership(GroupModel)} returns false" (it actually checks `canManageMembers`), and `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` documents "@return Stream of IDs of groups with view permission" although the method returns a `Set<String>`. Since these interfaces are the contract used by other modules (admin-ui-ext, services), the wrong text is likely to be copied into new implementations.

findings.title: No negative test that a view-only group permission does not grant manage
findings.body: `testViewGroups` creates an all-groups `VIEW` permission and only asserts that groups become visible. There is no assertion that this read-only permission does not allow write operations (creating a top-level group, updating a group, adding a child). Such an assertion would have caught that `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` returns `true` for the `view` scope, which currently lets a view-only admin create top-level groups. Similarly, no test exercises `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (all-groups `view-members` permission combined with `GET /users` and `GET /users/count`), which is why the id/name mix-up in that method goes unnoticed.
